messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: large increase in tail latency and token cost for /generate on pool-redwood-eu (starts 1793456760). p95 token time spike, continuous_batching queue growing. Pager triggered.
ryan_oncall: I'm on it. I'm seeing p95 -> 3.2s and token/sec cost up 4x. Root of spike around 1793456600.
anya_sre: paging in. Any deploys or config changes in the last hour? checking deploy bot...
infra-bot: Deploy: batch-config-service v2.3.1 deployed at 1793456523 to pool-redwood-eu. Rollout: 25% traffic.
marta_ml: That rollout contains the new continuous batching heuristics + prefix-kv rekeying. Could be related.
luke_pm: Customer-facing? Jenny, any CS hits?
jenny_cs: Customer @acme-retail reported timeouts on realtime search suggestions starting ~13:10 UTC. Several support tickets. Not full outage but severe degradation for power users.
ryan_oncall: Reproduced locally: when batching grows beyond 48 requests, KV prefix cache blows up memory and invalidates multiple prefixes, causing re-tokenization and long tails.
anya_sre: Interesting — logs show repeated prefix-invalidation events from batch-config-service with reason: "heuristic_key_mismatch".
marta_ml: That matches a tokenizer-normalization mismatch we saw in test when unicode normalizer changed from NFKC->NFC in a library bump. Could change hashing of prefix tokens.
anya_sre: Can we confirm the key mismatch? dumping a sample of prefix keys (redacted) now.
anya_sre: ```
# prefix keys (shortened)
old: kb1:pref:4f8a1e9d
new: kb1:pref:4f8b2f9d
# differing by 0x011 vs 0x01 in codepoints
```
marta_ml: looks like normalization difference. When keys change, prefix cache entries are not deduped -> memory balloon -> eviction cascades -> re-tokenize -> continuous-batching queues back up -> perf cliff.
ryan_oncall: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) rollback batch-config-service to 2.3.0 (prior heuristics) or 2) disable continuous_batching for the affected model pool. Which is faster?
anya_sre: Disabling continuous_batching on pool is faster (no deploy). We can push a config toggle via config service.
ryan_oncall: I'll flip the flag and monitor. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://config.internal/v1/pools/pool-redwood-eu/toggles \
  -d '{"continuous_batching_enabled":false, "reason":"incident 1793456789 - revert heuristics"}'
```
infra-bot: config change accepted, propagation to pool-redwood-eu started (1793456880).
anya_sre: Rolling metrics now... p95 decreased from 3.2s -> 1.1s in first 90s. Token rate trending back down.
jenny_cs: Noted improvement from customers - ACME says suggestions are coming back but slower for a few users.
luke_pm: Can we also do a targeted cache purge to remove orphaned keys and avoid a second wave when flag toggled back on?
marta_ml: Yes, we can run a safe prefix-sweep that normalizes keys to the older normalization form and removes unknown-key entries. I have a script.
anya_sre: Let's not purge everything. Plan: run script in dry-run on a single shard, confirm latency stable, then sweep others.
ryan_oncall: Handoff time in 20m. I'll document steps and ongoing checks.
ryan_oncall: RUNBOOK (copy):
1) Flag toggled: continuous_batching_enabled=false -> infra-bot shows propagation
2) Monitor p95 and token rate (grafana:pool-redwood-eu -> /generate route)
3) Run prefix-sweep dry-run on shard-03: 
```
python tools/prefix_sweep.py --shard shard-03 --normalize NFKC --dry-run
```
4) If dry-run shows <0.1% deletions and no latency blips, run without --dry-run across shards sequentially.
5) Re-enable batching only after QA validation and a coordinated deploy of tokenizer normalization fix.

anya_sre: Running dry-run now. Output:
```
shard-03: scanned 1.2M keys, normalized mismatch: 0.04% (480 entries), suggested deletions: 480
no latency increase during run
```
marta_ml: Good. That implies the memory blowup was from duplicates, not a wholesale codepath error.
jenny_cs: I'll message ACME with an interim update: "We've applied a mitigation reducing tail latency; a targeted cache sweep is in progress and we expect full recovery in ~45m. We'll follow up with a root-cause summary." :pray:
anya_sre: Proceeding with sequential sweep on other shards now. Running on shard-04.
infra-bot: prefix-sweep job shard-04 started at 1793456978.
anya_sre: shard-04 dry-run: 2.1M scanned, 0.06% mismatches, suggested deletions: 1260. No latency change.
anya_sre: After sweep across all shards, memory usage dropped 28% and continuous-batching queue flushed.
ryan_oncall: Before I hand off: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: tokenizer normalization changed in a dependency bump in batch-config-service v2.3.1 producing non-normalized prefix tokens; batch heuristics rekeying exacerbated duplicate keys -> KV cache blowups -> perf cliff.
marta_ml: Action items: (1) revert the tokenizer change in batch-config-service; (2) add a canonical normalization pass before hashing prefixes; (3) add unit/regression test for normalization; (4) add a safe failover to reject new prefix keys if aggregate prefix growth rate > X%/min.
luke_pm: I'll create a customer-facing summary once we validate root cause. Also schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow.
jenny_cs: ACME acknowledged interim update and is grateful.
ryan_oncall: Handoff to anya_sre for next 2hr watch. Notes: flag still false, sweep completed, monitor for reappearance. If any reappearance, page me.
anya_sre: Acknowledged. I'll keep watching dashboards and log alerts. Planning to open a PR with normalization fix and keep batching disabled until validated.
infra-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> investigating. Incident channel: #incidents. Incident id: 2026-1793456789.
marta_ml: Quick question: does anyone have a pointer to the exact dependency bump PR? I can start patching.
anya_sre: PR: github.com/redwood/batch-config-service/pull/542 (bump tokenizer lib 1.8.3 -> 1.9.0). I'll add notes.
ryan_oncall: Thanks all, handing off now. :wave:
anya_sre: Thanks, taking over. I'll file postmortem outline and assign owners.
luke_pm: Thanks team. Great coordination. :tada:
